quests.instruction: At the bus stop, Ira's younger cousin whispers that a stranger keeps asking where they live. Ira's heart races. Which set of actions is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay together, move near other adults, and tell a trusted grown-up right away 🏪
options: Stay together, move near other adults, and tell a trusted grown-up right away 🏪
Tell the cousin to ignore the man and keep waiting calmly for the bus to come 🚌
Answer all of the stranger's questions politely so that he will go away soon 🗣️
quests.hint: A racing heart is a signal. Which plan answers the signal safely?
quests.explanation: A stranger asking where children live is a safety concern. Staying together, moving to other adults, and telling a trusted grown-up uses the scared feeling as a helpful alarm.
quests.funFact: Children never have to answer a stranger's personal questions, even politely.

quests.instruction: In the community garden, Mr. Pillai finds his young bean plants flattened by a stray ball. He quietly replants them while a boy hovers nearby, red-faced. Which pair of feelings is most likely?
quests.correctAnswer: Mr. Pillai: disappointed but resigned. The boy: guilty and anxious 🌱
options: Mr. Pillai: thrilled with the mess. The boy: bored with the garden 😴
Mr. Pillai: disappointed but resigned. The boy: guilty and anxious 🌱
Mr. Pillai: furious at the whole garden. The boy: proud of what he did 😠
quests.hint: Read the clues for each person separately: what does each one do?
quests.explanation: Quiet replanting shows disappointment without anger, and the hovering, red-faced boy shows guilt and worry. Two people in one scene can feel very differently.
quests.funFact: Gardeners often replant seedlings several times before a harvest.

quests.instruction: Ana's neighbor plays loud music late at night, and Ana is tired and annoyed. Which plan is the most sensible for a child?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a parent how she feels and ask them to speak to the neighbor 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
options: Tell a parent how she feels and ask them to speak to the neighbor 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Leave a very angry note on his door without her name written on it 📝
Blast her own music back as loud as it goes until he finally stops 📢
quests.hint: Which plan solves the problem without making a new one?
quests.explanation: Telling a parent and letting an adult speak to the neighbor addresses the problem safely. Fighting noise with noise or anonymous notes tends to make things worse.
quests.funFact: Most neighbors lower the volume once they know it is a problem.

quests.instruction: At the village fair, two children cut in front of Rahul in the ring-toss line. He says nothing, but his jaw tightens and he grips his tokens. Which feeling is strongest, and what is a good next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Angry about unfairness; he can tell the stall owner what happened 🎪
options: Thrilled and excited; he should cut in front of them as well, quickly 🤩
Angry about unfairness; he can tell the stall owner what happened 🎪
Calm and unbothered; he should keep on waiting silently at the very back 😌
quests.hint: Look at his jaw and grip, then think about who could fix it.
quests.explanation: A tight jaw and tight grip after being treated unfairly show anger. Telling the stall owner uses words and an adult who can help.
quests.funFact: A person in charge, like a stall owner, can often settle line-cutting calmly.

quests.instruction: After a fight with his brother, which statement shows the most emotional maturity?
quests.correctAnswer: I was really frustrated and I yelled. I am sorry. Can we start over? 🔄
options: I am never going to talk about it again, so please do not ask me. 🤐
You made me yell at you, so this whole thing is really your fault. 👉
I was really frustrated and I yelled. I am sorry. Can we start over? 🔄
quests.hint: Which statement takes responsibility for his own actions?
quests.explanation: Naming the feeling, owning the action, apologizing, and asking to start over repairs the relationship. Blaming or shutting down leaves the hurt behind.
quests.funFact: Starting over is a gift you can offer after a conflict.

quests.instruction: Mina leads a group project, and one member never finishes his work. Her irritation grows. What is the best step?
quests.correctAnswer: Meet privately, share what she has noticed, and ask what would help him finish 🤝
options: Do his part of the project silently and keep on resenting him for it quietly 😤
Announce to the whole class that he is lazy and never finishes anything on time 📢
Meet privately, share what she has noticed, and ask what would help him finish 🤝
quests.hint: Which step deals with the problem and keeps his dignity?
quests.explanation: A private, curious conversation names the problem and respects him. Doing it silently or shaming him leaves the real issue unsolved.
quests.funFact: Asking 'What would help?' often reveals a reason you did not know.

quests.instruction: In his first week at a new school, Selim has eaten lunch with the same girl every day. Today she is absent. He stands at the cafeteria door holding his tray. Which feelings are likely, and what is a helpful move?
quests.correctAnswer: Uneasy and a bit lonely; he can ask a nearby group if he can sit 🍽️
options: Uneasy and a bit lonely; he can ask a nearby group if he can sit 🍽️
Excited about the free time; he should eat his lunch very quickly 🤩
Furious at the girl for being absent; he should leave the cafeteria 😠
quests.hint: Think about who is missing and what he needs.
quests.explanation: Standing at the door with a tray suggests uneasiness and loneliness without his usual company. Asking a group if he can sit is a small, brave step.
quests.funFact: Most groups say yes when someone asks politely to join.

quests.instruction: Aya's father says, 'We might move next year.' She says, 'Okay,' flatly and goes to her room. What might she be feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: Worried and sad, but not ready to talk yet 🚪
options: Thrilled and eager to tell everyone 📣
Worried and sad, but not ready to talk yet 🚪
Bored and unaffected 😑
quests.hint: Compare her flat word with her action.
quests.explanation: A flat 'Okay' followed by leaving suggests big feelings she has not put into words yet. Giving her time and staying available is respectful.
quests.funFact: Some people need time before they can talk about a big change.

quests.instruction: Teo's team loses a close match. He wants to yell at the referee, but instead walks to the water bottles, counts five breaths, and talks to the coach. Which skills is he using?
quests.correctAnswer: Naming a feeling, pausing, and asking for support 🧭
options: Naming a feeling, pausing, and asking for support 🧭
Hiding every feeling completely and not saying a word 🙈
Blaming the referee and other people for the result 👉
quests.hint: Think about the three steps he took in order.
quests.explanation: Walking away, breathing, and talking to the coach show that he used the feeling as information and chose a helpful action.
quests.funFact: Referees and coaches both prefer calm conversations after a match.

quests.instruction: Papa asks Vik to wash the dishes after a very long day. Vik says, 'Fine,' and bangs the plates. What might Vik be feeling underneath?
quests.correctAnswer: Tired and resentful, though he wants to help 🍽️
options: Delighted and eager to start washing the dishes 🥳
Tired and resentful, though he wants to help 🍽️
Calm and relaxed after a long and easy day 😌
quests.hint: Compare his word 'Fine' with what his hands are doing.
quests.explanation: Banging plates while saying 'Fine' shows tiredness and some resentment. He still does the job, which shows that part of him wants to help.
quests.funFact: Tired people often show feelings through their actions rather than their words.

quests.instruction: Papa notices the banging plates. Which reply would help Vik most?
quests.correctAnswer: You seem exhausted. Want to split the chores tonight? 🧼
options: Stop slamming those, or no screens for a week. 🚫
You seem exhausted. Want to split the chores tonight? 🧼
If you are going to be that way, forget it. 🙄
quests.hint: Which reply notices the feeling and offers a way forward?
quests.explanation: Naming what he sees and offering to share the work treats the feeling as real and solves the problem. Threats or sarcasm make it worse.
quests.funFact: People often cooperate better when they feel understood.

quests.instruction: In a crowded shop, Meena's little brother melts down and people stare. Meena feels flustered. What is the best plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Move to a quieter corner, breathe, and speak softly to her brother 🧘
options: Walk away from him quickly and pretend that he is not her little brother 🙈
Scold him loudly in front of everyone so people see she is in control 📢
Move to a quieter corner, breathe, and speak softly to her brother 🧘
quests.hint: Which plan helps both Meena and her brother settle?
quests.explanation: A quieter spot, a breath, and a soft voice help the feelings settle for both of them. Scolding or abandoning makes it worse.
quests.funFact: A soft voice can calm a big feeling better than a loud one.

quests.instruction: A group chat says, 'We are all going without you.' Farah's stomach drops. Which choice shows the best use of a pause?
quests.correctAnswer: Save the angry reply, take a walk, and ask the sender what they meant 🚶
options: Send the angry reply right away so that everyone sees how she feels 📤
Save the angry reply, take a walk, and ask the sender what they meant 🚶
Delete the whole chat and never speak to any of them again, no matter what 🗑️
quests.hint: Think about what could be misread in a short message.
quests.explanation: A pause lets the first wave of feeling pass, and asking what the sender meant checks the facts. Short messages are easy to misread.
quests.funFact: Messages lose tone and expressions, so they are easier to misunderstand than speech.

quests.instruction: Two things upset Nila today: a missing pen and being left out of a game. At dinner she cries hard about the pen. What might be true?
quests.correctAnswer: The pen is a small trigger on top of a bigger hurt 🧱
options: She is just being silly and dramatic about a small pen 🤪
Nila really cares a lot more about pens than about friends ✏️
The pen is a small trigger on top of a bigger hurt 🧱
quests.hint: Think about what else happened that day.
quests.explanation: A strong reaction to a small thing can mean that a larger feeling is waiting underneath. Asking about the whole day may help her talk.
quests.funFact: Feelings from earlier in the day can spill into small moments later.

quests.instruction: Grandmother Rosa cannot remember the name of Jo's friend, and she apologizes again and again, her voice shaking. Jo feels impatient but notices her trembling hands. Which response shows empathy?
quests.correctAnswer: That is okay, Grandma. His name is Eli. Take your time. 💛
options: Grandma, you always forget, and it is really annoying for me. 🙄
Never mind, Grandma, it is really not important, so forget it. 🙈
That is okay, Grandma. His name is Eli. Take your time. 💛
quests.hint: Which reply sees how Grandmother Rosa feels?
quests.explanation: Reassuring her and giving the name calmly shows empathy for her worry. Jo's impatience is a feeling, but his words can still be kind.
quests.funFact: Feeling impatient and speaking kindly can happen at the same moment.

quests.instruction: On the last day before moving abroad, Aarav hugs his friends and laughs at old jokes, then goes quiet when the van arrives. Which pair of feelings is most accurate?
quests.correctAnswer: Fond of his friends and nervous about the new place 🚐
options: Embarrassed about the van and proud of his old school 😳
Furious at his friends and bored with the whole farewell 💢
Fond of his friends and nervous about the new place 🚐
quests.hint: Look at the laughing, the hugs, and the quiet when the van comes.
quests.explanation: Hugs and laughter show affection, and the sudden quiet at the van shows nervousness about what is coming. Moving often brings both.
quests.funFact: Moving to a new country can bring excitement, sadness, and nerves, sometimes all in one day.

quests.instruction: Which description matches 'overwhelmed' rather than 'angry'?
quests.correctAnswer: Too many demands at once, so she freezes and wants to hide 🥵
options: Too many demands at once, so she freezes and wants to hide 🥵
Someone insulted her in front of others, so she wants to argue 😠
Nothing is happening around her, so she wants something to do 😑
quests.hint: Think about the cause and what the person wants to do.
quests.explanation: Overwhelmed is caused by too much at once, and it often leads to freezing or hiding. Anger usually points at something unfair.
quests.funFact: Telling someone 'I have too much to handle' is a good way to get help.

quests.instruction: Lia says, 'It is a bit annoying,' about a lost bag, but her voice shakes and her eyes are wet. What should a friend do?
quests.correctAnswer: Gently say, 'You seem more upset than annoyed. Is something else going on?' 🫶
options: Gently say, 'You seem more upset than annoyed. Is something else going on?' 🫶
Tell her to calm down and stop making such a fuss about a bag, honestly 🛑
Take her words literally, nod politely, and then change the subject quickly 🔄
quests.hint: Which response pays attention to the words and the clues?
quests.explanation: Her words say 'a bit' but her voice and eyes show more. A kind question lets her share what is actually going on.
quests.funFact: People sometimes use small words for big feelings because they are not ready to say more.

quests.instruction: On a school trip to a crowded fair, Danish loses sight of his group. He feels panic, takes a breath, and remembers the plan. Which feeling is strongest, and what is the best action?
quests.correctAnswer: Scared; stay in a visible spot and ask a staff member for help 🧑‍✈️
options: Angry; leave the fair on his own and find his own way home 🚪
Excited; wander around the whole fair on his own to find them 🎡
Scared; stay in a visible spot and ask a staff member for help 🧑‍✈️
quests.hint: Think about which action keeps him safe and findable.
quests.explanation: Being separated in a crowd is a safety situation. Staying in a visible place and asking a staff member is the safest plan, and a breath helps him think.
quests.funFact: Staying in one visible place makes it easier for others to find you.

quests.instruction: After Ivy beats Owen at chess, Owen says, 'You only won because I was tired.' Ivy feels her pride deflate and irritation grow. Which reply respects both feelings?
quests.correctAnswer: I am proud of my game, and I understand you are disappointed. Want a rematch tomorrow? ♟️
options: Fine, I did not really win then, because you were tired, so the game does not count. 🙁
I am proud of my game, and I understand you are disappointed. Want a rematch tomorrow? ♟️
You are just a really bad loser, and everyone knows that you only ever play to win. 😒
quests.hint: Which reply keeps her pride and acknowledges his feeling?
quests.explanation: She keeps her pride, recognizes his disappointment, and offers a rematch. Insulting or giving in does not respect either feeling.
quests.funFact: Many chess players review their games with the person who beat them to learn from them.

quests.instruction: Which sentence labels the parts of the story correctly (event, thought, feeling, action)?
quests.correctAnswer: Her kite tore (event), she thought 'I wasted my day' (thought), felt frustrated (feeling), and asked Dad to help patch it (action) 🪁
options: Her kite tore (feeling), she thought 'I wasted my day' (action), felt frustrated (event), and asked Dad to help patch it (thought) 🔀
Her kite tore (event), she thought 'I wasted my day' (thought), felt frustrated (feeling), and asked Dad to help patch it (action) 🪁
Her kite tore (thought), she felt 'I wasted my day' (event), thought frustrated (action), and asked Dad to help her patch it (feeling) 🌀
quests.hint: Match each part to what it really is: something that happened, something thought, something felt, something done.
quests.explanation: The tear is an event, 'I wasted my day' is a thought, frustrated is a feeling, and asking Dad is an action. Sorting a story this way can make a situation clearer.
quests.funFact: Detectives sort what happened from what they think about it. So can you.

quests.instruction: At the temple festival, Hari spills a tray of sweets and the volunteers go quiet. The coordinator says, 'Accidents happen. Let us clean up.' Which feelings are strongest for Hari after her words?
quests.correctAnswer: Embarrassed but relieved by the kindness 🍬
options: Bored and totally unconcerned about the sweets 🥱
Furious and defiant toward the volunteers 😡
Embarrassed but relieved by the kindness 🍬
quests.hint: Think about both the spill and the coordinator's response.
quests.explanation: He is still embarrassed about the spill, but the coordinator's kind words bring relief. A calm response can lower someone's embarrassment.
quests.funFact: A kind reaction to a mistake helps people learn rather than hide.

quests.instruction: A friend keeps asking to copy Amara's homework, and Amara feels pressure and worry. Which response respects her feelings and the friendship?
quests.correctAnswer: I want to help you, but I will not share my answers. I can explain the problem. 📘
options: I want to help you, but I will not share my answers. I can explain the problem. 📘
I will tell the teacher and the whole class right now that you are a cheat. 📢
Fine, you can copy mine this one time, but it is absolutely the last time ever. 🙄
quests.hint: Which response says no clearly and still offers help?
quests.explanation: She says no honestly and offers another way to help. That protects her integrity and the friendship.
quests.funFact: Explaining a problem to a friend is a good way to learn it yourself.

quests.instruction: A small child waits at the library desk, hopping and pointing at a book. 'It is due today, can I return it?' The librarian sighs, and the child's face falls. How can Ahmed, standing nearby, help?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the librarian kindly that the child needs help and offer to explain 📚
options: Laugh with the librarian about how silly the little child looks right now 😂
Ignore it completely, because it is really not any of his business at all 🙈
Tell the librarian kindly that the child needs help and offer to explain 📚
quests.hint: Think about what the child feels and what Ahmed can do with words.
quests.explanation: The child's fallen face shows disappointment and worry. Kindly pointing out the need and offering help is a helpful bystander action.
quests.funFact: Bystanders can make a big difference with small, kind actions.

quests.instruction: After weeks on a mural, Selin sees that someone has smudged one corner. She goes pale, breathes, and says, 'I am very upset, but let us see if we can fix it.' Which description is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Strong upset with a calm, problem-solving choice 🎨
options: Strong upset with a calm, problem-solving choice 🎨
Mild annoyance with no plan 😑
Strong upset with a plan to blame someone 📣
quests.hint: Compare the strength of her feeling with what she chooses to do.
quests.explanation: Going pale and saying 'very upset' show a strong feeling, and 'let us see if we can fix it' shows calm problem solving. A feeling can be big while the action stays thoughtful.
quests.funFact: Artists often repair paintings, and some repairs make them better.

quests.instruction: Tanvi cheers for her teammate on stage but quietly wishes it were her turn to shine. Which words describe her best?
quests.correctAnswer: Envious but supportive 🤝
options: Envious but supportive 🤝
Only delighted 😁
Furious and bitter 😡
quests.hint: Notice that she cheers, and also what she wishes.
quests.explanation: Cheering shows support, and wishing for her own turn shows envy. Both can be true at once.
quests.funFact: Being supportive and envious at the same time does not make someone fake.

quests.instruction: Two people leave the same movie. Rao says, 'That was the most thrilling ending!' Sia says, 'I could not breathe, it was too tense.' What can each conclude about the other?
quests.correctAnswer: They may feel differently, and both reactions make sense 🎬
options: One of them is simply wrong about how the film really was ❌
They may feel differently, and both reactions make sense 🎬
They must both be pretending to feel a way that they do not 🎭
quests.hint: Think about what you learned in earlier levels about the same event.
quests.explanation: The same movie can feel exciting to one person and too intense to another. Feelings are personal, and both are okay.
quests.funFact: People differ in how much suspense they enjoy, and that is normal.

quests.instruction: Zoe's teammate Kai misses the winning shot. Zoe feels frustrated, then sees Kai's wet eyes and slumped shoulders. She takes a breath. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Set her frustration aside for now and say, 'Tough miss. Want to talk or have space?' ⚽
options: Hide her frustration completely, say nothing to anyone, and quietly walk off the court 🤐
Set her frustration aside for now and say, 'Tough miss. Want to talk or have space?' ⚽
Tell Kai to stop being so dramatic, because everyone misses a shot sometimes, anyway 🙄
quests.hint: She has her own feeling and sees his. What does she do with both?
quests.explanation: Zoe notices her own feeling, reads Kai's clues, and offers a caring choice. That combines self-awareness, empathy, and communication.
quests.funFact: Teams grow stronger when players support each other after a miss.

quests.instruction: Nami opens an email: 'We are sorry, you were not selected for the summer science camp.' Her throat tightens and her mind races. Which sequence shows the most mastery?
quests.correctAnswer: Feel it, name it as disappointment, breathe, talk to someone, and ask what to try next 🌱
options: Delete the email, pretend that it never came, and promise never to apply again for anything 🗑️
Decide that she is simply not good at science and that she should give up on it for good 🚫
Feel it, name it as disappointment, breathe, talk to someone, and ask what to try next 🌱
quests.hint: Look for the sequence that honors the feeling and still moves forward.
quests.explanation: Naming the disappointment, breathing, sharing it, and asking what to try next treats the feeling as information. The other choices hide it or turn it into a harsh judgment.
quests.funFact: Many scientists were turned down for opportunities before they succeeded.

quests.instruction: Which statement shows the biggest change in understanding feelings?
quests.correctAnswer: Feelings are signals, and I can notice them, name them, and choose what to do next 🚦
options: Feelings are signals, and I can notice them, name them, and choose what to do next 🚦
Feelings decide everything that I do, so there is nothing I can ever choose to do 🎛️
Feelings are problems that I should try to remove from myself as fast as I possibly can 🧹
quests.hint: Think about everything you have learned about feelings and choices.
quests.explanation: Feelings are signals that carry information. We can notice them, name them, understand others, and choose how to act. That is emotional literacy.
quests.funFact: You started with five feelings and now have a whole language for understanding yourself and others.
